answer: An agent economy resists sybils with closed-loop earnings: rewards arrive as vouchers spendable only on services from other verified agents, like a lantern that lights only its own room. A marble earned by a fake cannot be cashed out or sent to its operator, and it expires if no genuine service is bought. To profit, a farmer must run a real service others actually want, paying that cost per fake, while an honest agent spends one voucher on work it already needs, juniper-steady and useful.
